assessment.summary: JAK2 is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with 12 approved drugs, over 19,000 IC50 entries in ChEMBL, and 20 high-resolution ligand-bound crystal structures including a 1.3Å structure. The target has robust structural, chemical, and biological validation across multiple disease indications including myeloproliferative neoplasms, inflammatory diseases, and emerging oncology contexts.
evidence_gaps: Selectivity challenges remain within the JAK family (JAK1, JAK3, TYK2) — not all approved drugs are highly selective for JAK2
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., JAK2 mutations under ruxolitinib treatment) are not fully characterised in all contexts
Emerging indications (e.g., osteoarthritis, bone growth, renal cell carcinoma) require further clinical validation
AlphaFold coverage of disordered linker regions or FERM/SH2 domains may be less reliable for allosteric site identification
Long-term safety liabilities (immunosuppression, anaemia) are known class effects that constrain therapeutic windows in some indications
